mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a short-term discounting effect that reduces expected future cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during periods of Fed rate hikes (p > 0.05), or the FEDFUNDS rate does not cross the 4% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 5.0% coincides with higher labor market uncertainty, which elevates risk premiums and depresses S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.0% in the current month
failure_condition: During UNRATE > 5% periods, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the effect is explained by other variables.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly index of industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 112.0 for two consecutive months, it signals a strengthening supply-side momentum that is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 out of 20 such windows (p > 0.05), or INDPRO remains below 112.0 for the next 60 days after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer demand proxy HOUST suggests weakening overall economic momentum, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
regime_hint: Dual contraction in supply and demand indicators
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when both proxies move in opposite directions or show no co-movement.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL inflation (three consecutive months below 2.0%) reduces the real discount rate, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days in a non-stagflation regime.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 out of 20 such inflation periods, or inflation re-enters >2.0% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in employment (PAYEMS) by more than 10,000 jobs in a month coincides with lower risk aversion and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10,000 in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive during such employment spikes (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent in non-shock months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in consumer demand measured by HOUST below 1000 units in a month, in conjunction with falling RSAFS, indicates a demand contraction that predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 1000 and RSAFS < previous month in the same period
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both proxies show contraction (p > 0.05), or the contraction is not persistent.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) both show upward momentum (each rising for two consecutive months), it signals a dual expansion that is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rising for two consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL rising for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 out of 20 such dual-expansion windows (p > 0.05), or momentum in one variable is absent.
